public_headline: Astronaut Cooper Reported Glowing Particles During 1963 Orbital Flight
public_tldr: This is an auto-transcribed audio excerpt from NASA's Mercury-Atlas 9 mission on 15 May 1963, in which astronaut Gordon Cooper described luminous white-green particles drifting away from his spacecraft in low Earth orbit. The particles were the same 'fireflies' phenomenon first reported by John Glenn on an earlier Mercury mission.
public_narrative:
On 15 May 1963, astronaut L. Gordon Cooper Jr. was orbiting Earth alone aboard Faith 7, the final mission in NASA's Mercury programme. At one hour and 21 minutes into the flight, he reported seeing what he called "John's fireflies" — a reference to the luminous particles first observed by astronaut John Glenn during his Mercury-Atlas 6 mission the previous year.

Cooper described the particles as white with a greenish tint, drifting rearward from his spacecraft. He was in a transitional lighting period — approaching daytime but still able to see stars distinctly overhead, while Earth's clouds below were changing colour and becoming lighter.

This document is an auto-transcription of Cooper's in-flight audio, released by NASA as part of a UAP-related disclosure. It captures a single astronaut's real-time observations, with no ground-based corroboration included in the excerpt. NASA's metadata attributes the phenomenon to frozen condensation from the spacecraft, though Cooper himself does not offer that explanation in the transcript.

The transcript shows no signs of significant redaction. However, auto-transcription has introduced likely errors — phrases such as "light rail fireflies" and "This guy looks dark" appear to be mishearings rather than Cooper's actual words.
public_caveats: This is a single-observer account from a solo mission — no crew member or ground station corroborates the visual details in this excerpt.
The transcript is auto-generated from audio, so specific wording may contain transcription errors that distort Cooper's original statements.
The official explanation (frozen condensation) comes from NASA metadata, not from anything Cooper says in the transcript itself.
The 'fireflies' phenomenon was already known from John Glenn's earlier mission and was not treated as unexplained by NASA at the time.
